contract: Native non-chat activation inventory. Required sets are terminal-owner closure, not endpoint counts. Every alias listed on a consumer must satisfy that consumer's conformance contract. Source states are observations, never runtime registrations or permission. Conformance test IDs below are obligations, not claims that those tests exist or passed. Matching evidence is not activation approval: publication separately qualifies prerequisites and retains current native writer fences. Maintainer-reviewed scope revision 2026-10-20 explicitly excludes native scheduled publication for now; future design is preserved in the main repository dev/backlog/scheduling.md. Reminders, scheduled reconciliation and existing queued delivery retain their separate obligations. Exclusion is not implemented scheduling or passing conformance.

modes.notes: Local resource-read overlay and lifecycle kernels exist. Complete native activation registrations and terminal conformance evidence do not exist. Mutation owners must retain current qualification/policy/subject fences through commit; disclosure owners have a bounded final handoff, not byte recall.

No native remote receiver contract is implemented. Every effect retains its full embedded alias closure plus remote.receiver. Private disclosure and mutations require online operation-bound permits and receiver cutoff; public snapshots require complete gap-free freshness. No embedded fallback.

effects.closure: Publication is a state transition across in-scope event/session/resource/form/commerce/import/AI aliases. It also reaches already queued publication handoffs and public derivatives. Native scheduled publication is explicitly excluded by the maintainer-reviewed 2026-10-20 scope revision and preserved in main-repository dev/backlog/scheduling.md; this does not exclude reminders, reconciliation or existing queued delivery. A controller-only or event-only set would leave native alternate publishers and queued work open.

New upload restriction covers generic and AI images and dedicated resource reserve/finalize paths. Cancel and replay remain required because cleanup and committed-result responses must neither reacquire rights nor disclose protected resource metadata.

A protected resource can escape through audience detail/page/actions, management detail/list/audit/export, private payload, redirect headers, upload success/replay metadata and generic storage fallback. Derived discovery/calendar/queued channels must suppress protected resource material too; they cannot register only an HTTP metadata check.

Management includes direct native and machine/AI operations, current membership and actor surfaces, resource management, event/session/form/commerce state and participant approval/transfer. Qualified sanction mutation remains a nonrecursive control-plane operation, not a blanket management bypass.

Actual participant restrictions must survive account/guest start, continuation, free/paid finalization, approval, claim, reassignment, transfer and provider callbacks. Existing entitlements need exact per-participant settlement and final credential/payment effects; payer or companion identity never substitutes for the affected participant. Physical Admission remains a separate effect.

Physical exclusion binds the actual participant at issuance, transfer, recovery and every single/batch scan, and settles affected entitlements without cancelling companions. Private location/resource derivatives must not disclose barred logistics from old credentials. This does not infer physical exclusion from a mere Publish or Participate restriction.

Private logistics can be returned directly, embedded in resource metadata/files/redirects, calendars, credentials or queued messages. Management and upload responses are not exempt. Public derivatives must not accidentally carry private logistics. This effect changes disclosure, not financial entitlement or physical admission.

New provisioning/continuity prohibition spans native identity provisioning, linkage/replacement, membership admission, service/delegation enrollment and guest-account claim. Recognition capture is separately prerequisite-gated; existing restricted accounts must still authenticate for protected remedies.

Protected status is positively owned control-plane disclosure, not a restrictable sanction capability. Status and safe final notices must remain accessible without exposing case evidence or using recursive generic evaluation.
Protected complaint eligibility, independent review, safe claimant status and revision-bound correction form one remedy path; generic support sessions or event-report intake cannot stand in for it.

Qualified support requires verified recovery/claimant authority, safe status and the same revision-bound correction writer. It is not an instance-admin allow-all route and not blocked by the generic evaluator.

Ordinary erasure remains independently accessible through its retained authority/saga/receipt owner. Recognition is not silently made mandatory for ordinary erasure; when Enrollment continuity is adopted its separate exact set includes identity.continuity and the same erasure owner.
